Abstract
In cloud computing, task scheduling has become more and more important for 
maximizing resource allocation, cutting down on energy use, and enhancing 
system performance. However, traditional algorithms often fall short in dynamic 
environments, leading to performance inefficiencies. For cloud computing energy 
efficiency, this research suggests a hybrid task scheduling method that combines 
Transformer-based fine-tuning and Cuckoo Search (HCS) optimization. The integration 
of bio-inspired optimization (HCS) and Modified BERT-Based Transformer allows 
for dynamic task reallocation, enhancing both energy consumption and resource 
utilization while maintaining high Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance. 
Fine-tuning with Transformer models enables adjustments to improve scheduling 
efficiency and minimize energy wastage. The results show that the proposed method 
reduced energy consumption to 0.430 J (from 0.440 J) while maintaining 100% SLA 
compliance and task completion rate. Resource utilization improved to 88.2%, with 
energy efficiency of 0.0043 J/task. This hybrid approach offers significant advantages 
over traditional methods, such as BENBO + Bi-LSTM (0.687 J), PSO-PGA (0.617 J), and 
GAECS (0.537 J), achieving a reduced energy consumption of 0.440 J for 15 PM with 
20 VMs, making it an ideal solution for scalable cloud computing environments.

Conventional heuristic-based scheduling methods tend to be incapable of handling

slowly in highly dynamic environments [20]. On the other hand, deep learning models, 
especially Transformer-based architectures, are excellent in learning historical patterns 
from scheduling data and adapting to workload changes [3]. A hybrid approach combin­
ing metaheuristic search algorithms with deep learning techniques can be developed to 
exploit both sides, for global optimization with metaheuristics and for intelligent deci­
sion-making with deep learning [29]. This would generally enhance the accurate sched­
uling of tasks, reduce computational overhead, and significantly save energy in cloud 
computing [21].
Hybrid Cuckoo Search and Transformer models combine very well in order to opti­
mize the task scheduling for cloud computing [5]. Cuckoo Search (CS) is a metaheuristic 
algorithm based on the brood parasitism behavior of the cuckoo bird [24]. This approach 
utilizes Lévy flights for exploring the solution space [4]. The CS has its superiority in the 
global optimization aspect but, for complex scheduling problems, might get stuck for 
too long a period [30]. Hybrid Cuckoo Search enhances its performance by incorporat­
ing more local search mechanisms, adaptive step sizes or other optimization techniques 
like hybridizing with other methods to ensure the rapid convergence and quality exploi­
tation of high-quality solutions [32].
On the other hand, attention to Transformer models in scheduling has been gained 
because of their great success in natural language processing, driven by a self-attention 
mechanism which enables learning dependencies between tasks and resources more

process scheduling constraints and predict optimal allocations without being affected 
by dynamic workloads in real time [23]. The combination of HCS for global search-

consumption, and overall improved performance of cloud services [10]. Utilizing the 
publicly available ‘Cloud Computing Performance Metrics’ dataset [14], which simulates 
real-world cloud workloads, to validate the proposed model’s energy efficiency and SLA

2  Related works
2.1  Deep learning-based scheduling approaches
This section highlights task scheduling techniques that utilize deep learning models 
such as CNN, LSTM, DRL, and Transformer architectures for improved adaptability and 
decision-making.

edge computing. Considering makespan, execution time, cost, and risk probability. They 
used the deep convolution neural network (D-CNN) to estimate risk probability based 
on the security of the task and VM. According to the simulation result, improved exe­
cution cost, time, and risk probability at 37.27, 0.99 s, and 0.19% over existing models, 
respectively. Oyelade et al. [26] proposed LSTM-based deep learning integration with 
metaheuristic algorithms, enhancing the quality of solution and speeding up conver­
gence. In this model, the historical optimization data, including the sequences of solu­

space. Under the experiment on 55 benchmark functions, including CEC 2017, it sur­
passed 13 traditional algorithms in solution quality and the degree of convergence rate.

energy efficiency and resource utilization in the cloud computing. The authors intro­
duced a new policy that maximizes rewards for task scheduling actions, which was

Sheikh et al. [33] suggested a machine learning-based task scheduling algorithm for

3  Problem statement
Cloud computing has changed the nature of modern computing through scalable and 
on-demand resource allocation. Despite these advances, however, scheduling remains 
a very important challenge for efficiency, with increasingly complex workloads and an 
optimum use of resources. Inefficiencies resulting from poor scheduling include high 
energy consumption, higher operational costs, and SLA violations.
Major problems in task scheduling:
Dynamic Workload Variations – Cloud systems experience frequent changes in task 
volume and priority, requiring real-time adaptability [33].
High Energy Consumption – Non-optimized task allocation can lead to overprovi­
sioning or resource contention, increasing power usage(Gupta and Agarwal 2022).
Resource Allocation Issues – Static or heuristic scheduling often results in either 
underutilized or overloaded VMs [5].
SLA Compliance- Inability to meet time-bound service requirements due to delayed 
or inefficient scheduling leads to SLA violations [28].
The framework proposed in this research is the hybrid scheduling approach that inte­
grates two algorithms, HCS Algorithm. This metaheuristic optimization method will 
enable efficient exploration of the scheduling space and minimize energy consumption. 
An AI-driven Deep Learning Model which uses Transformer-based approach for priori­
tizing the tasks based on workload patterns and adaptive scheduling.
Research Objectives.
 	•
Design a Hybrid Task Scheduling Model to optimize task allocation in cloud 
computing.
 	•
Minimize energy consumption by optimizing resource utilization while maintaining 
high performance and meeting SLA requirements.
 	•
Enhance scheduling accuracy and adaptability by leveraging the self-attention 
mechanism of Transformers to learn workload patterns and dynamically adjust to 
cloud environment fluctuations.
 	•
Optimize resource utilization by ensuring balanced workload distribution across 
virtual machines (VMs), preventing both overloading and underutilization of 
resources.
HCS is well-suited for addressing large-scale, multi-objective optimization problems 
such as task scheduling, due to its global search capabilities and ability to avoid local 
minima through Lévy flight-based exploration. Meanwhile, Transformer models, partic­
ularly when fine-tuned, offer strong contextual learning capabilities, making them ideal 
for dynamically adjusting task assignments based on patterns in workload, resource 
status, and priority. The combination of these two methods enables both broad optimi­
zation and adaptive fine-tuning, making the hybrid approach highly effective in energy-
sensitive, SLA-constrained cloud environments.

4.3.1  Overview of CSA

the bio-inspired optimization method known as Cuckoo Search (CS) was inspired by

this case, the cuckoo has to adapt to a new strategy for nest selection. In computer sci­
ence, the solution space for optimization issues is explored and exploited using this nat­
ural selection concept. CS features Levy flight-based random walk, which is a stochastic

4.3.2  Hybrid enhancements in HCS
While the standard CSA is efficient in terms of global optimization, it cannot be used to 
fine-tune a solution on a local level, thereby affecting the scheduling precision. Thus, a 
Hybrid Cuckoo Search model that incorporates an adaptive step size with local search

and enhances scheduling efficiency.

The value of the step size ααα is adjusted dynamically in accordance with the workload

Interpretation of Results The decrease in energy consumption with the proposed 
model demonstrates the efficacy of using bio-inspired optimization and DL together. The 
hybrid strategy is superior to conventional scheduling methods, which registered higher 
energy consumptions. Dynamically changing task allocation based on workload priority 
and energy efficiency, the model maximizes both performance and resource usage.
Limitation and Future Works This work is mainly centered on energy-efficient task 
scheduling and doesn’t cover privacy-preserving mechanisms, e.g., Secure Aggregation, 
that are relevant in federated or multi-tenant cloud scenarios. Moreover, the existing 
model is trained off-line, which can cause model staleness for very dynamic environ­
ments. Personalized scheduling or user-specific SLA variations are not supported by the 
framework; thus, it is not as adaptable for heterogeneous user cases. In addition, com­
munication overhead in peak-demand scheduling can cause latency, and hardware het­
erogeneity is not yet incorporated in the simulated environment.
Future research will investigate the incorporation of Secure Aggregation methods 
to enable federated or privacy-conscious scheduling and online learning for real-time 
adaptability. Extensions to accommodate personalization, fault tolerance, and deploy­
ment in multi-cloud and edge computing environments will be taken into account to 
make the proposed framework more robust and scalable.
Implications and Significance The findings of this research hold important impli­
cations for managing resources in cloud computing. Through the optimization of task 
scheduling to minimize energy consumption, cloud service providers can lower their 
operational costs and enhance sustainability. The method can also be extended to other 
areas, including edge computing or IoT systems, where energy efficiency and resource 
management are highly important. Another benefit of using Transformer models is their 
built-in explainability due to attention mechanisms. From examining attention weights, 
cloud administrators can understand which tasks the model gives preference to or 
assigns resource allocation based on aspects such as the level of task urgency, the load 
of resources, or SLA demands. This interpretability enhances improved troubleshoot­
ing, transparency, and trustworthiness of automated scheduling systems, making the

6  Conclusion
This paper proposes a hybrid task scheduling framework that integrates Hybrid Cuckoo 
Search (HCS) with a Transformer model to maximize energy efficiency and resource uti­
lization in cloud computing. Besides showing excellent performance in simulated set­
tings, the proposed approach indicates promise for real-time adaptability on different 
workload priorities. Its potential to ensure SLA adherence, enhance resource utilization 
efficiency, and minimize energy cost per task implies great applicability in energy-aware 
cloud data centers and scalable infrastructure.
The modular structure of the model renders it appropriate for extension to multi-cloud 
setups and edge computing situations, where dynamic management of resources is impor­
tant. Additionally, its combination of optimization and learning-based improvement 
presents a solid starting point for future intelligent cloud orchestration research. Adding 
real-time feedback loops, fault tolerance, or federated optimization would enhance robust­
ness and generalizability further. These developments could create the seeds for greener, 
more autonomous clouds in line with sustainability objectives. Outside of cloud environ­
ments in the traditional sense, the envisaged HCS–Transformer hybrid scheduling frame­
work has immense potential for use in cutting-edge paradigms like fog computing and 
mobile edge computing (MEC). The paradigms have comparable challenges dynamic work­
loads, scarce energy budgets, and latency-critical tasks whereby adaptive and power-aware 
scheduling is of enormous value. Using the context-awareness of the Transformer and the 
global optimization of HCS, the model can be generalized to decentralized and heteroge­
neous environments, allowing for smart task distribution in distributed edge-fog networks.

Abstract: In cloud computing, task scheduling has become more and more important for maximizing resource allocation, cutting down on energy use, and enhancing system performance. However, traditional algorithms often fall short in dynamic environments, leading to performance inefficiencies. For cloud computing energy efficiency, this research suggests a hybrid task scheduling method that combines Transformer-based fine-tuning and Cuckoo Search (HCS) optimization. The integration of bio-inspired optimization (HCS) and Modified BERT-Based Transformer allows for dynamic task reallocation, enhancing both energy consumption and resource utilization while maintaining high Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance. Fine-tuning with Transformer models enables adjustments to improve scheduling efficiency and minimize energy wastage. The results show that the proposed method reduced energy consumption to 0.430 J (from 0.440 J) while maintaining 100% SLA compliance and task completion rate. Resource utilization improved to 88.2%, with energy efficiency of 0.0043 J/task. This hybrid approach offers significant advantages over traditional methods, such as BENBO + Bi-LSTM (0.687 J), PSO-PGA (0.617 J), and GAECS (0.537 J), achieving a reduced energy consumption of 0.440 J for 15 PM with 20 VMs, making it an ideal solution for scalable cloud computing environments.
